discovery: Discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductors and the theory of their multiband sign-changing (s+-) pairing

nominees.name: Hideo Hosono
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Science Tokyo (formerly Tokyo Institute of Technology), Japan

motivation: In 2008 Hideo Hosono discovered superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. Within months, related iron pnictides and chalcogenides were found with transition temperatures above 50 K. This was the first family of high-temperature superconductors since the cuprates, and it was based on iron, an element long thought to be hostile to superconductivity. Igor Mazin quickly proposed that pairing in these materials is unconventional: an s+- state whose gap changes sign between electron and hole Fermi pockets, driven by spin fluctuations. Neutron spin-resonance, quasiparticle-interference and impurity experiments later confirmed this specific, falsifiable prediction. The iron-based materials showed that intrinsically multiband superconductivity, with several coupled order-parameter components, is a general route to high transition temperatures. They have become the main experimental platform for multicomponent phenomena, including nematicity, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking states and fractional vortices, and they reshaped our understanding of unconventional superconductivity.
